::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 12th 1864  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 36-7
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd),
We are at home at last and in three days more I hope to send up the copy for the printer of all the ancient history [Golden Deeds](cmy_books/cmybook_51.qmd).[^1] Of course he will let me have the proofs. I hope the delay will not prove to have been of consequence. Are there to be any vignettes to the chapters, if there are, there is a story of the Coliseum which quite asks for one of the Dying Gladiator or of the Coliseum itself. I think there should be a chronological index, the ground of which I will make before sending up these sheets of the M S.

Thanks for sending me [Karamsin](other_books/otherbook_366.qmd), which arrived on Saturday, it looks so full of interest that we should like to make it our <u>pièce de resistance</u> for our winter’s reading if you can let us keep it long enough.

[My brother](people/person_1624.qmd) desires me to ask whether you would like to have him translate Todleben’s [Sebastopol](other_books/otherbook_368.qmd)which was reviewed in the Times the other day.[^2]

I suppose your Isle of Wight holiday is over. Ours has ended by an arrival in a house with only two habitable rooms

Yours very truly
C. M. Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: Each of the deeds is dated and 'ancient history' probably means the first fourteen chapters, the last of which was dated 404 A.D.
[^3]: The review was by [William Howard Russell](people/person_1270.qmd).  JBY was presumably offering to translate from the French rather than the Russian edition.
